# Step 6c: the archived Step-5d transport, replayed through the audio path.
#
# The captures are not in the repository and are not captured again. They are
# the Step-5d acceptance archive, and their identity - name, size, SHA-256 -
# lives in testdata/psi-hardware/manifest.txt and nowhere else. This file adds
# cases only, so that the two steps can never disagree about which bytes a
# result came from.
#
# A run resolves each name under XG2G_AUDIO_HARDWARE_DIR and refuses to proceed
# unless the bytes hash to what the Step-5d manifest says.
#
# Chunk sizes are packet counts times 188: 65424 is 348 packets. A chunk
# boundary can only fall between packets, and PES packets still straddle them,
# which is the point.

version 1

# Each capture on its own, at the programme Step 5d resolved for it.
case R-orf1hd
  target 4911
  chunk 65424
  feed A_orf1hd
end

case R-orf1hd-second
  target 4911
  chunk 65424
  feed A2_orf1hd
end

case R-puls4
  target 20007
  chunk 65424
  feed B1_puls4
end

case R-schlager
  target 35
  chunk 65424
  feed B2_schlager
end

# A zap, on one core. Three programmes in sequence, so the incarnation
# boundaries are drawn on real transport rather than on authored packets - and
# the audio of the programme that was left cannot reach the observers of the
# one that arrived.
case R-zap
  target 4911
  chunk 65424
  feed A_orf1hd
  settarget 20007
  feed B1_puls4
  settarget 4911
  feed A2_orf1hd
end

# The interruption cases. Production destroys the parser when the upstream ends
# and builds a new one for the next connection, so the boundary is a new core
# and not a gap in the bytes.
case R-reconnect
  target 4911
  chunk 65424
  feed H_pre
  newcore
  feed H_post
end

case R-reboot
  target 4911
  chunk 65424
  feed I_pre
  newcore
  feed I_post
end
